complete_examples.text: In the present study, a novel time-frequency analysis approach is put forward by inte-grating wavelet transform and Wigner-Ville distribution, through which track irregularity can be represented as a function of spatial position, amplitude and wavelength, and be characterized by time-frequency energy densities (TFEDs) in time-frequency domain.
Therefore, in present study, wavelet transform and SP-WVD are united to properly improve the reliability of the results.

In this practical model, the increment and iteration methods are introduced and integrated into the static mapping analysis to solve the nonlinear interlayered contact and separation, and subsequently, to achieve dynamic mapping analysis under a VTS dynamics framework, besides, the Wavelet transform is applied to obtain the more distinct observation signal in the time domain.

Similarly, utilizing the Wavelet transform to obtain the low-frequency signal, as shown in Fig. 10, the filtered signal has an obvious mapping relationship with the second derivative of irregularity shown in Fig. 10d. Therefore, it can be concluded that the low-frequency components of wheelset acceleration are relative to the corresponding second derivative of additional irregularities which is unlike the static mapping relationship, and due to this conclusion, further studies are carried out.

Combining wavelet transform’s multi-resolution analytical characteristics and Wigner-Ville distribution’s high time-frequency energy-focusing performance, a wavelet-SPWVE time-frequency algorithm of locating and extracting track irregularity wavelength was proposed and compared with the conventional scale-wavelet energy spectrum analysis method.
